questions.statement: Choose the correct article: 'She is ___ engineer who works on bridges.'
questions.context: Semana W24 de ingles, grado 11: ejercicio 1 de 20 sobre the articles a, an and the.

options.text: an
options.feedback: Correct! 'Engineer' begins with a vowel sound, so the indefinite article takes the form 'an'.

options.text: a
options.feedback: No. 'A' is used before a consonant sound, and the vowel sound of 'engineer' rules it out.

options.text: the
options.feedback: No. 'The' would point to a specific engineer already identified by the listener.

options.text: no article
options.feedback: No. Every singular countable noun needs an article in English, so leaving it out is not possible here.

questions.explanation:
'Engineer' begins with a vowel sound, so the indefinite article takes the form 'an'. In this item the choice that works is 'an', because it is the option that matches what the sentence and the task require.

questions.statement: Which sentence uses 'the' correctly for something the listener already knows about?

options.text: Look at the tower; it is the tallest one in the town.
options.feedback: Correct! 'The tower' points to a specific tower already mentioned, and 'the tallest' identifies a unique member of a group.

options.text: Look at a tower; it is a tallest one in the town.
options.feedback: No. 'A tower' introduces something new, which is not the meaning of 'look at' pointing to a known object.

options.text: Look at tower; it is the tallest one in the town.
options.feedback: No. A singular countable noun cannot appear without an article in English.

options.text: Look at the tower; it is a tallest one in the town.
options.feedback: No. 'A tallest' contradicts the superlative, which is already definite and takes 'the'.

questions.explanation:
'The tower' points to a specific tower already mentioned, and 'the tallest' identifies a unique member of a group. In this item the choice that works is 'Look at the tower; it is the tallest one in the town.', because it is the option that matches what the sentence and the task require.
